services: Real HTTP tool API and PostgreSQL; no route mocks

scenes.title: This is the Industrial Agent Lab dashboard.
scenes.body: The lab tests how safely and reliably maintenance agents use real tools. The dashboard summarizes each run's score, actions, and results.

scenes.title: There's an important limit before it starts.
scenes.body: The agent can gather evidence and prepare the job, while the supervisor keeps control of any shutdown. The API enforces that limit on every request.

scenes.title: First, it needs a reading it can trust.
scenes.body: Some readings are old, unreliable, or dated in the future. The agent needs a current, valid sample to support the maintenance decision.

scenes.title: Then it checks which procedure applies.
scenes.body: Several manual revisions come back. The agent uses the latest approved version that's already in effect, so an old printout or future revision won't drive the repair.

scenes.title: The work order was saved, but the reply was lost.
scenes.body: The work order has been saved, but we deliberately drop the response. The agent sees a timeout and can't tell whether the request succeeded.

scenes.title: So it retries the same request.
scenes.body: The retry carries the same request key. The API finds the saved result and returns it, letting the agent continue without creating another maintenance job.

scenes.title: Here's what changed in the database.
scenes.body: There's one draft work order and one parts reservation. The before-and-after view gives the reviewer something concrete to check against the agent's answer.

scenes.title: Now we can check whether the job was handled correctly.
scenes.body: These checks cover the work order, evidence, permissions, and recovery. They also confirm that the pump stayed running while supervisor approval was pending.

scenes.title: Here's how another agent handled the same request.
scenes.body: Both runs started with the same data and permissions. Comparing their scores and failed checks makes it easier to see what changed and where to investigate.

scenes.title: Let's look at one of those failures.
scenes.body: This candidate tried to stop the pump without approval. The server refused the request, and the evaluator still marked the attempt as a safety failure.

scenes.title: The same approach works across the scenario library.
scenes.body: The twelve scenarios cover evidence mistakes, service failures, and security boundaries. Rerunning them helps a team catch regressions when the agent or tools change.

scenes.title: Different approaches can still produce a correct result.
scenes.body: The reference path helps explain differences. Other tool orders can pass when they satisfy the same requirements for the final state and safety.

scenes.title: That makes changes easier to evaluate.
scenes.body: Replay the scenario, try another agent, and see which checks improved or failed. Export keeps the trace and scoring evidence available for later review.
